The '''Allegheny County Jail''' is the municipal [[Prison|jail]] of [[Allegheny County, Pennsylvania|Allegheny County]], located at 950 Second Avenue in [[Pittsburgh|Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]]. The current facility, completed in 1995, replaced the old jail, which is attached to the [[Allegheny County Courthouse]] and now serves court functions.

== History ==

=== Old jail ===
{{See also|Allegheny County Courthouse}}
The old Allegheny County Jail was part of a complex (along with the [[Allegheny County Courthouse]]) designed by [[Henry Hobson Richardson|H. H. Richardson]]. The buildings are considered among the finest examples of the Romanesque Revival style for which Richardson is well known.

The jail was built by the [[Norcross Brothers]] between 1884 and 1886 (the year of Richardson's death), and the courthouse was finished in 1888 under the supervision of [[Shepley, Rutan and Coolidge]].  The two structures are linked across Ross Street by a "Bridge of Sighs" (so called for its similarity to the [[Bridge of Sighs|famous bridge]] in [[Venice, Italy]]).  Additions were made 1903{{ndash}}1905 by [[Frederick J. Osterling]].

In 1892, [[anarchist]] [[Alexander Berkman]] was held here awaiting trial for the attempted murder of [[industrialist]] [[Henry Clay Frick|H. C. Frick]]. In 1902, condemned brothers [[Jack and Ed Biddle]] escaped from the jail with the aid of the warden's wife.

The jail and courthouse were added to the [[List of City of Pittsburgh historic designations]] on December 26, 1972.<ref name="CPHS">{{cite web | url=http://www.phlf.org/historic-plaque-program/local-historic-designations/ | title=Local Historic Designations | publisher=Pittsburgh History & Landmarks Foundation | location=Pittsburgh | accessdate=2011-08-11| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20110721004051/http://www.phlf.org/historic-plaque-program/local-historic-designations/| archivedate= 21 July 2011 | url-status= live}}</ref>  They were added to the [[List of National Historic Landmarks in Pennsylvania|List of National Historic Landmarks]] on May 11, 1976. After its 1995 closing, most of the building was renovated to become the Allegheny County [[family court]], while a small section of a cell block has been preserved as a museum dedicated to the history of the jail.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allegheny County Family Courts Facility {{!}} Mascaro |url=https://www.mascaroconstruction.com/projects/allegheny-county-family-courts-facility/ |access-date=2025-06-29 |website=Mascaro Construction Company, LP |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Smerker |first=Nick |date=2022-06-03 |title=PHLF: Old Allegheny County Jail Museum |url=https://alleghenywest.org/phlf-old-allegheny-county-jail-museum/ |access-date=2025-06-29 |website=Allegheny West |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== New jail ===
Due to crowded and insecure conditions at the old jail, the current Allegheny County Jail opened on April 29, 1995, at a cost of $147 million, after 29 months of construction. The five- to eight-story building was designed by L. Robert Kimball & Associates and [[Tasso Katselas]] Associates, and won a citation from the joint committee of the [[American Institute of Architects]] and the [[American Correctional Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-29 |title=ON THIS DAY: April 29, 1995, New $147M Allegheny County Jail opens |url=https://www.wpxi.com/archive/this-day-april-29-1995-new-147m-allegheny-county-jail-opens/MUWWWOVN5ZA4RFUCJPTQRMGWX4/ |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=WPXI |language=en}}</ref> It houses 1,800 cells, and although its original capacity was set at 1,850, the county puts its capacity at over 3,000. Its population varies from day to day, and mostly remains under 1,800.<ref>{{Cite web |title=County Jail |url=https://www.alleghenycounty.us/Government/County-Jail |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=www.alleghenycounty.us |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Allegheny County Jail |url=https://www.andrew.cmu.edu/course/90-740A/pres3/sld016.htm#:~:text=The%20Allegheny%20County%20Jail%20was,about%2016%25%20of%20property%20taxes. |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=www.andrew.cmu.edu}}</ref> It is situated next to the campus of [[Duquesne University]] (Katselas intended for the waterfront view of the jail to complement and echo the university's Old Main), and sited on a 17-acre "peninsula" surrounded by highways on all sides.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allegheny County Jail |url=https://www.tassokatselas.com/allegheny-county-jail |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=www.tassokatselas.com}}</ref>

According to a 1996 Pennsylvania Department of Corrections report, the jail lacked "formal leadership" already shortly after its opening.<ref name=":0" /> Controversy surrounding the jail has continued to the present, through the terms of several wardens. Particular concerns have been raised regarding new use-of-force training,<ref name="WESAcriticism">{{cite web |date=September 1, 2021 |title=Warden Responds To Criticism Over Allegheny County Jail's Use Of Force Training, Weapons Contracts |url=https://www.wesa.fm/post/warden-responds-criticism-over-allegheny-county-jail-s-use-force-training-weapons-contracts |publisher=90.5 WESA}}{{Dead link|date=September 2023|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> unsanitary living conditions,<ref name="MSNcriticism">{{cite web|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/allegheny-county-jail-warden-receiving-criticism-after-survey-releases/ar-AAM7bEU|title=Allegheny County Jail Warden receiving criticism after survey releases|publisher=MSN}}</ref> the jail's death rate,<ref name="PPGmisled">{{cite web|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/opinion/2022/07/19/Bethany-Hallam-Allegheny-County-Jail-Warden-Orlando-Harper-has-misled-the-public-again/stories/202207190033|title=Bethany Hallam: Allegheny County Jail Warden Orlando Harper has misled the public again|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|date=July 19, 2022}}{{dead link|date=July 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> insufficient mental and health care,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2025-01-28 |title=Trevor Wingard takes over as warden at Allegheny County Jail |url=https://www.wesa.fm/courts-justice/2025-01-28/trevor-wingard-takes-over-as-warden-at-allegheny-county-jail |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=90.5 WESA |language=en}}</ref> and persistent disputes between jail administration and the [[Prison officer|correctional officer's]] union.<ref name="WPXIcontroversies">{{cite web|url=https://www.wpxi.com/news/top-stories/allegheny-county-jail-warden-addresses-recent-controversies/2PK5SC2U7BBY3I3IGJRC4P42FE/|title=Allegheny County Jail warden addresses recent controversies|publisher=WPXI}}{{Dead link|date=September 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref><ref name="Survey">{{cite news |date=2021-06-15 |title=Correctional officers blast ACJ working conditions in new survey |url=https://www.pghcitypaper.com/news/cp-jail-watch-correctional-officers-blast-acj-working-conditions-in-new-survey-24167390 |accessdate=2023-07-15 |work=Pittsburgh City Paper}}</ref> In light of these concerns, the county is attempting to reduce the jail's population by methods including diversion to treatment programs and wider use of "alternative housing" outside of the jail.<ref name=":1" />

In May 2023, a group of protestors rallied against the conditions at the Allegheny County Jail.<ref name="Protest">{{cite news |date=2023-05-13 |title=Protesters march Downtown over conditions at Allegheny County Jail |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/news/crime-courts/2023/05/13/protest-downtown-pittsburgh-allegheny-county-jail-conditions-inmates/stories/202305130073 |accessdate=2023-07-16 |work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette}}</ref> The police reported an assembly of 50 to 60 people on the 400 block of Grant Street, Downtown, shortly before 2:30 PM. The protestors then marched down Fifth Avenue. According to a flyer, the gathering was sponsored by the Alliance for Police Accountability. The 2025 arrival of warden Trevor Wingard, who promised to shake up the jail's "status quo", was met with cautious approval from the Alliance.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-08 |title=Advocates 'hopeful' about change under Allegheny County Jail warden nominee |url=https://www.wesa.fm/courts-justice/2025-01-08/allegheny-county-jail-warden-nominee-trevor-wingard |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=90.5 WESA |language=en}}</ref>

== Jail Oversight Board ==
The '''Jail Oversight Board''' of Allegheny County is a statutory body that oversees the operation and maintenance of the Allegheny County Jail and its alternative housing facilities. The board's responsibilities also include overseeing the health and safekeeping of its incarcerated residents, and the confirmation of the County Executive's selection of a warden.<ref name="Jail Oversight Board">{{Cite web|url=https://alleghenycontroller.com/the-controller/jail-oversight-board/|title=Jail Oversight Board|publisher=Allegheny County Controller}}</ref>

The board is composed of nine members, including elected officials, judges, and citizen members. These members are:
* The County Chief Executive
* Two judges of the Court of Common Pleas
* The County Sheriff
* The County Controller
* The President of County Council
* Three citizen members.<ref name="Jail Oversight Board" />

Meetings are held at least once per month, usually on the first Thursday, in the Gold Room of the Allegheny County Courthouse. These meetings are open to the public and are streamed live on [https://www.youtube.com/@alleghenycountyjailoversig5127/streams YouTube].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.alleghenycourts.us/general-information/jail-oversight-board/|title=General Information: Jail Oversight Board|publisher=Allegheny County Courts}}</ref> The public can submit comments or questions online prior to the meetings or sign up for public comment before each meeting.

In addition to regular meetings, the board receives monthly reports on various aspects of the jail's operations, such as segregated housing, use of force, deaths, grievances, and health care.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.alleghenycounty.us/uploadedFiles/Allegheny_Home/Dept-Content/Jail/Docs/Reports/JOB%20Segregated%20Housing%20Report%20December%202022.pdf|title=Segregated Housing Report December 2022|publisher=Allegheny County}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.alleghenycounty.us/uploadedFiles/Allegheny_Home/Dept-Content/Jail/Docs/Reports/JOB%20Segregated%20Housing%20Report%20June%202023.pdf|title=Segregated Housing Report June 2023|publisher=Allegheny County}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.alleghenycounty.us/uploadedFiles/Allegheny_Home/Dept-Content/Jail/Docs/Reports/JOB%20Segregated%20Housing%20Report%20November%202022.pdf|title=Segregated Housing Report November 2022|publisher=Allegheny County}}</ref>

Community-based coalition the Corrections Collective provides resources and support for incarcerated individuals, their families, and communities affected by arrest and incarceration.<ref name="Jail Oversight Board" />

Public access to records and documents regarding the Board and Allegheny County Jail is provided by the Controller's Office. This includes meeting minutes, the warden's monthly reports, and other jail-related records.<ref name="Jail Oversight Board" />

== List of wardens ==
The following individuals have served as warden of the Allegheny County Jail since its opening:
* Leonard Dever (1995–2005)<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/local/city/2005/02/18/Jail-warden-resigns-after-decade-of-service/stories/200502180189|title=Jail warden resigns after decade of service|date=February 18, 2005|publisher=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette}}{{dead link|date=July 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
* Calvin Lightfoot (2005–2007)<ref name="Jail warden resigns">{{Cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/local/city/2007/03/06/Jail-warden-resigns/stories/200703060156|title=Jail warden resigns|date=March 6, 2007|publisher=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette}}{{dead link|date=July 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
* Ramsey Elias (2007–2010)<ref name="Jail warden resigns" />
* Daniel Onorato (interim, 2010)<ref name="post-gazette.com">{{Cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/local/city/2014/01/23/Allegheny-County-Jail-warden-resigns/stories/201401230241|title=Allegheny County Jail warden resigns|date=January 23, 2014|publisher=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette}}{{dead link|date=July 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
* Ramon Rustin (2010–2014)<ref name="post-gazette.com" />
* Orlando Harper (2014–2023)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.alleghenycounty.us/jail/staff/warden.aspx|title=Orlando L. Harper, Warden|publisher=Allegheny County Bureau of Corrections}}</ref>
* Shane Dady (2023–2025)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wtae.com/article/allegheny-county-interim-jail-warden-dady-harper/45195300 |title=Interim Allegheny County Jail warden announced |date=18 September 2023}}</ref>
* Trevor Wingard (2025–present)<ref name=":1" />

== In popular culture ==

The 1984 film [[Mrs. Soffel]], based on the escape of the [[Jack and Ed Biddle|Biddle brothers]], includes shots of the jail exterior and then-interior scenes. Over the three days of filming at the jail, some prisoners were used as extras. The jail was featured in the 2010 film ''[[The Next Three Days]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=On Location: Allegheny County Jail |url=https://www.pittsburghmagazine.com/on-location-allegheny-county-jail/ |website=Pittsburgh Magazine |date=10 June 2021 |access-date=13 February 2025}}</ref>

The old Allegheny County Jail has been used in many other movies, including [[The Silence of the Lambs (film)]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mavrogianis |first=Alexa |date=2016-07-26 |title=10 Things You Might Not Know About The Old Allegheny County Jail |url=https://www.pittsburghmagazine.com/10-things-you-might-not-know-about-the-old-allegheny-county-jail/ |access-date=2026-07-12 |website=Pittsburgh Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>
